q: Which mountain range runs like a giant backbone across Morocco?
explain: The Atlas Mountains stretch across Morocco and its neighbours in northwest Africa.

q: Ethiopia is famous as the birthplace of which popular drink?
explain: Legend says coffee was discovered in Ethiopia after a goat herder saw his goats become lively from the berries.

q: Ghana is one of the world's biggest growers of which crop, used to make chocolate?
explain: Ghana is one of the world's top cocoa growers, and cocoa beans are what chocolate is made from.

q: Which giant hot desert covers most of Algeria?
explain: The Sahara, the world's largest hot desert, spreads across the whole southern part of Algeria.

q: Which ancient city, home of the general Hannibal, stood where Tunisia is today?
explain: Carthage was a powerful ancient city near modern Tunis, famous for Hannibal and his war elephants.

q: Which ocean washes the western coast of Senegal?
explain: Senegal sits on Africa's westernmost bulge, right beside the Atlantic Ocean.

q: Which big-eyed primates live in the wild almost only on the island of Madagascar?
explain: Lemurs live in the wild only on Madagascar, apart from a couple of kinds on the nearby Comoros islands that people probably brought there long ago.
